laws.heading: Nandi County: no alcohol for under 18s
laws.rule: Nandi County Alcoholic Drinks Control Act, 2014, s 32: no person may sell, supply or provide an alcoholic drink to a person under 18. The penalty is a fine of up to KES 150,000 (about A$1,639; A$1 = KES 91.49 (CBK rate KES 129.96 per USD, 29 Oct 2026, with RBA A$1 = USD 0.7040, 30 Oct 2026)) or up to 1 year in prison, or both. A seller has a defence if they asked to see an age document and believed on reasonable grounds that it was genuine. The Act also bars under-18s from the part of licensed premises where alcohol is made, stored, sold or consumed. A person under 18 found buying or drinking alcohol can be sent to compulsory counselling and rehabilitation (s 32).
laws.penalty_signal: Up to KES 150,000 (about A$1,639) or 1 year for the seller

laws.heading: Nandi County: where and when alcohol can be sold or drunk
laws.rule: Nandi County Alcoholic Drinks Control Act, 2014, s 38 (breach of licence): except as the Act provides, no person may sell alcohol in a workplace, office, factory, public park, public recreational facility, public transport vehicle, public beach, sports stadium or public street, and no person may sell, buy or drink alcohol at a selling outlet after the hours for which the outlet is licensed. For selling without the right licence, a first offence carries a fine of up to KES 1,000,000 (about A$10,930) or up to 1 year in prison, or both. Licence hours are set in the Act's Schedule and were not extracted; ask the outlet or check the Act.
laws.penalty_signal: Fines and imprisonment under the county Act
